amendments.rule: The definite direct-object marker `אֵת` (H853) has no English realization of its own and is normally its own `unrepresented` unit; that is the ruling on the large majority of its occurrences. It takes English only where the ASV spends a word on the object relation itself and no other morpheme licenses that word. Four families qualify. An English verb may reach its object through a preposition — *hearken unto*, *spake unto*, *inquire of*, *fight against*, *send for* — where that preposition exists only to attach the object to the verb; it is the marker's rendering, not the object noun's, and the marker heads on it. An appositional or resumptive marker may be rendered *even* or *to wit*. **But only a marker standing on the very phrase that English word introduces.** Where the ASV writes an appositional *even* or *to wit* before a phrase no marker marks, no morpheme licenses it and it is its own `added` unit under rule 30, whatever markers stand elsewhere in the clause: `וְחַקּוֹתָ עָלֶיהָ עִיר אֵת־יְרוּשָׁלִָם` → *portray upon it a city,* ***even*** *Jerusalem* gives *even* to the marker, which stands on the appositive itself, while `נָתַתִּי לְךָ אֵת־שְׁנֵי עֲוֺנָם לְמִסְפַּר יָמִים שְׁלֹשׁ־מֵאוֹת וְתִשְׁעִים יוֹם` → *a number of days,* ***even*** *three hundred and ninety days* leaves the *even* `added`, because the clause's one marker stands on `שְׁנֵי עֲוֺנָם`, which the ASV renders bare. Do not reach across the clause for a marker to carry such a word, for the reason rule 42 gives about a surplus *and*: the word is written beside those renderings rather than inside one of them. And a marker on an object the ASV fronts before its clause and resumes inside it with a pronoun may be rendered *as for*: `וְאֶת־הַיְבוּסִי יוֹשְׁבֵי יְרוּשָׁלִַם לֹא־יָכְלוּ בְנֵי־יְהוּדָה לְהוֹרִישָׁם` → *And* ***as for*** *the Jebusites the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the children of Judah could not drive them out* gives *as for* to the marker, headed on *as* by rule 24, since the resuming *them* is the suffix's under rule 18 and nothing else answers to the two words. **The same limit governs that third family.** Where the ASV writes *as for* before a fronted phrase no marker stands on, no morpheme licenses the expression and it is its own `added` unit under rule 30, headed on *as*: `וּמַרְאֵיהֶם דְּמוּת אֶחָד לְאַרְבַּעְתָּם` → *And* ***as for*** *their appearance, they four had one likeness* leaves the *as for* `added`, because `מַרְאֵיהֶם` is a bare noun and suffix with no marker and no preposition on it. Do not fold the expression into the fronted noun to avoid the `added`, for the reason just given about a surplus *even*, and do not reach for rule 33: that rule gives a supplied function word to a noun whose own case-function licenses it, and a topicalized nominal's fronting is not such a case-function. Where a morpheme does stand on the fronted phrase it takes the expression, whether that morpheme is a marker as above or a fronting `לְ` — `לָאוֹפַנִּים לָהֶם קוֹרָא` → ***As for*** *the wheels, they were called* gives *As for* to the `לְ` under rule 11. **And a marker on a direct object the ASV demotes to a role phrase takes the preposition written for it.** Where the ASV recasts the marked object as the role the thing serves and writes a supplied *for* or *as* before it, promoting the object's appositive to the English verb's object — `וְהֵבִיא אֵת־קָרְבָּנוֹ שְׂעִיר עִזִּים` → *he shall bring* ***for*** *his oblation a goat* — that word is the marker's and it heads on it, since the marked noun keeps its own English and nothing else in the clause answers for the preposition. Rule 33 is what governs the same clause written without a marker, and it says so in its own terms: a nominal with no preposition and no object marker on it takes the supplied word itself, as `וְהֵבִיא קָרְבָּנוֹ` → ***for*** *his oblation* and `יָבִיא קָרְבָּנוֹ` → ***as*** *his oblation* do. So read whether a marker stands on the noun before placing the word, and do not leave it `added`: one of the two morphemes always licenses it. Test by subtraction: drop the English word and ask which morpheme has lost its rendering. If nothing but the object relation is diminished, the marker takes the word; if the ASV writes the object bare — *he built the house* — the marker is `unrepresented`. Do not confuse H853 with its homograph the preposition `אֵת` *with* (H854), which is an ordinary preposition aligning by rule 11.
amendments.why: LEV.4.23, 4.28 and 4.32 write the same clause three times, twice without a marker on `קָרְבָּן` and once with one, and the ASV writes a supplied *for* or *as* before the noun each time. Rule 33's own condition — a nominal with no preposition and no object marker on it — excludes the markered case, and rule 16's three families did not reach it, so the word had no licensor and would have fallen to `added` against the evidence of a morpheme standing exactly where the English preposition stands. The corpus already aligns the marker to *for* in 24 units, so the family is attested rather than invented. The added text is narrow: it governs a marked object the ASV demotes to a role phrase, states the rule 33 boundary in both directions, and leaves the subtraction test and the unrepresented default untouched.

conventions: The offering chains mizbah ha-olah, meqom ha-olah, zevah ha-shelamim and qetoret has-sammim fall under rule 29's fronting branch, not its supplied branch. The ASV renders the rectum anarthrously (of burnt offering, of peace offerings, of sweet incense), so the the it writes for the chain is fronted and belongs to the article on that rectum, and the construct takes no supplied the. Where the chain is multi-level and the ASV writes two the's (the base of the altar of burnt offering, the ox of the sacrifice of peace offerings, the horns of the altar of sweet incense), the article takes the inner one and the outer construct keeps the second as its supplied one. Contrast the arthrous chains of this chapter, where the ASV writes a the before the rectum's own word (the head of the bullock, the blood of the sin offering, the fat of the lamb): there nothing is fronted and the construct's the is the supplied one.

For any one of the commandments, count the phrase's determiner morphemes against the ASV's determiner words as rule 42 counts waws against and's. Where kol stands on the noun it takes the any and the numeral ahat is unrepresented (4.13); where the ASV writes both any one and all, ahat takes any one and kol takes all (4.22); where no kol stands, ahat takes the any (4.27); and where a partitive min stands before the numeral and the ASV writes any one of them, the first min takes any, ahat takes one and the second min takes of (4.2). nefesh takes any one whole where no numeral stands (4.2) and only any where one does (4.27). Each such unit names the competing reading.

hevi et-qorbano -> bring for his oblation gives the for to the object marker (4.23), while the same clause without a marker gives the supplied for or as to qorban itself under rule 33 (4.28, 4.32). Read whether a marker stands on the noun before placing the word; neither reading leaves it added.

kaasher rendered by the single word as is one rule 30 unit whose source head is the comparative preposition ke, not the relative asher. The chapter takes that reading at 4.10, 4.20, 4.21, 4.31 and 4.35 and names the relative as the competing head.

Three lexical pairs fuse under rule 30 in this chapter: ben baqar -> young (4.3, 4.14), seir izzim and seirat izzim -> goat (4.23, 4.28), and be-shegagah -> unwittingly (4.2, 4.22, 4.27), the last of which the ASV may front away from its clause position (4.22). tamim and temimah are not fused: they take without blemish whole, headed on blemish.

The recast commandment phrase miswot YHWH asher lo teasenah -> the things which Jehovah hath commanded not to be done gives the whole the things ... hath commanded to miswot, headed on commanded under rule 31, while the divine name keeps only the name it is recast as subject with. Uniform at 4.2, 4.13, 4.22 and 4.27.

report: Real split, fixed: a construct chain whose arthrous rectum the ASV renders anarthrously was analysed two ways. In LEV.4.12 (kol ha-par -> the whole bullock), 4.24 and 4.33 (ha-olah -> the) and 4.27 (am ha-arets -> the common people) the present article takes the written the that English fronts. In LEV.4.7, 4.10, 4.18, 4.25, 4.26, 4.29, 4.30, 4.31, 4.34 and 4.35 the same operation was inverted: the construct took that the as a supplied one and the article went unrepresented under the note 'No the before burnt offering'. Nothing in the source licenses the difference, and rule 29 settles it (kur ha-barzel -> the furnace of iron; 'Mark the article unrepresented only where the ASV writes no the for the phrase at all'). Thirteen articles across ten verses are patched.

Multi-level chains follow rule 29's levav kol bene ha-adam clause: the article takes the inner written the and the second written the stays the outer construct's supplied one. So in yesod mizbah ha-olah -> the base of the altar of burnt offering only the altar pair moves, the base is untouched; likewise shor zevah ha-shelamim -> the ox of the sacrifice of peace offerings and qarnot mizbah qetoret ha-sammim -> the horns of the altar of sweet incense.

Checked and left alone, because the source or the ASV licenses the difference: any / any one / all across nefesh, ehad, kol and min in 4.2, 4.13, 4.22 and 4.27, each phrase's determiner morphemes counted against the ASV's determiner words (rule 15 with rule 42's counting, competing readings already named in the unit notes); et taking for on a marked qorban in 4.23 against rule 33 giving for and as to the bare qorban in 4.28 and 4.32; shahat recast as a passive in 4.15 against the supplied they of 4.24 and 4.33; the added it after put and burn wherever no object morpheme stands (4.17, 4.19, 4.25, 4.30, 4.31, 4.34) against the suffix taking them in 4.35; min rendered in for dipping in 4.17 where 4.6 writes be; the wide spread of al and el renderings, all read off the ASV.

BSB: no genuine error. The R x5, Td x16 and To x14 groups are the documented convention difference on prepositions, articles and object markers. The four named singletons are all defensible under the contract: 4.9 nah is an object suffix the ASV does not render (rule 22), 4.12 and 4.21 la is silenced by the mi-huts fusion (rules 30, 40), 4.13 ahat loses its determiner to the kol standing on the noun (rule 15), 4.23 waw has no connective written for it (rule 14). The Td disagreement count falls from 16 to 3 as a by-product of the rule 29 correction; that is corroboration under rule 7 and was not the reason for it.

Not audited here, but worth a look: mizbah ha-olah and zevah ha-shelamim recur throughout Leviticus and Exodus, so LEV.1-3 and EXO.40 may carry the same inverted reading. That is outside this chapter's unit of work under rule 10; I have not touched them.

Conventions logged: the rule 29 fronting reading for these offering chains, the determiner count for any one of, the marked-versus-bare qorban pair, the ka-asher head choice, the three lexical fusions, and the isshey YHWH head. Amendment returned for rule 16, which had no home for the for the ASV writes before a marked object it demotes to a role phrase.
